6.1 came out the next day, on 5 August 2026 (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`), with a patch for each, the security archive says (`docs/releases/security.txt`), and 6.1.1 lists no security fix.
`strip_tags` parses the text and repeats while a pass still removes a tag; the `striptags` filter calls it (`django/utils/html.py:strip_tags`).
An end tag now pops the stack of open tags only when it closes the tag opened last (`django/utils/text.py:TruncateHTMLParser.handle_endtag`).

`wrap`, behind `wordwrap`, was open to very long strings (CVE-2025-26699, 5.0.13 and 5.1.7); at this commit it hands each line to `textwrap.TextWrapper` (`django/utils/text.py:wrap`; [Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`](../utils/text.md)).

`wrap`, behind `wordwrap`, was open to very long strings (CVE-2025-26699, 5.0.13 and 5.1.7); at this commit it hands each line to `textwrap.TextWrapper` (`django/utils/text.py:wrap`; [Text helpers: `Truncator` and `django/utils/text.py`](../utils/text.md)).

It now returns its input as given when the decimal's digits and its exponent's absolute value come to more than 200: `"1e199"` is written out in 200 digits, `"1e200"` left alone (`django/template/defaultfilters.py:floatformat`; [The built-in filters](../templates/filters.md#numbers)).
The number formatter writes a decimal past the same cutoff in scientific notation (`django/utils/numberformat.py:format`).

6.0.8 hands it a `decimal.Decimal`, so that a string holding a float, which `int` cannot read, gets the locale's format too, as the docstring now says (`django/contrib/humanize/templatetags/humanize.py:intcomma`; [Humanize: `naturaltime`, `intcomma` and the other filters](../contrib/humanize.md#the-numbers)).
Python's NFKC normalization, which `urllib.parse.urlsplit` can perform, is slow on Windows (`docs/releases/5.2.12.txt`).
The guards here stop a long URL before it is split, at `MAX_URL_LENGTH`, 2,048 characters (`django/utils/http.py`).

At this commit a word longer than `MAX_URL_LENGTH` once its punctuation is trimmed is left as text, and the trimming counts a word's brackets once (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.handle_word`, `django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.trim_punctuation`).

At this commit a word longer than `MAX_URL_LENGTH` once its punctuation is trimmed is left as text, and the trimming counts a word's brackets once (`django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.handle_word`, `django/utils/html.py:Urlizer.trim_punctuation`).
The widget links only a value `URLValidator` accepts, which refuses one over the bound before splitting it (`django/contrib/admin/widgets.py:AdminURLFieldWidget.get_context`).

Each judges its redirect with `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`, which refuses a URL over `MAX_URL_LENGTH`, a relative path too, before splitting it; the two auth views then take their default target, and `set_language` the `"Referer"` or `"/"` (`django/utils/http.py:_url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`, `django/views/i18n.py:set_language`; [The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](../http/helpers.md#urls-that-came-from-a-client)).

Each judges its redirect with `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`, which refuses a URL over `MAX_URL_LENGTH`, a relative path too, before splitting it; the two auth views then take their default target, and `set_language` the `"Referer"` or `"/"` (`django/utils/http.py:_url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme`, `django/views/i18n.py:set_language`; [The helpers in `django/utils/http.py`](../http/helpers.md#urls-that-came-from-a-client)).

The form field's `URLField.to_python` split the value to decide whether to put a scheme in front (CVE-2026-25673, 5.2.12 and 6.0.3); it now looks only at what precedes the first colon (`django/forms/fields.py:URLField.to_python`).

`HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__` raises `DisallowedRedirect` past `MAX_URL_REDIRECT_LENGTH`, 16,384 characters, before splitting the target (`django/http/response.py:HttpResponseRedirectBase.__init__`; [The response object](../http/response.md#redirects)).

`is_valid_ipv6_address` and `clean_ipv6_address` now refuse text longer than `MAX_IPV6_ADDRESS_LENGTH`, 39 characters, before `ipaddress` parses it, and `django.forms.GenericIPAddressField` passes on 39 unless given another max_length (`django/utils/ipv6.py:_ipv6_address_from_str`; [Dates, durations and addresses: `parse_datetime`, `parse_duration` and `clean_ipv6_address`](../utils/parsing.md#ipv6-addresses-clean_ipv6_address)).

It now cuts a code longer than `LANGUAGE_CODE_MAX_LENGTH`, 500 characters, at its last hyphen within the limit, and refuses one with no hyphen there, or any when `strict=True` (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:get_supported_language_variant`).

At this commit it refuses a code over the limit, and asks the cached `translation_catalog_exists`, which holds up to 1,000 codes, about the rest (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:check_for_language`; [Choosing a language: `LocaleMiddleware`](../i18n/choosing.md#whether-a-catalogue-exists)).

`ASGIRequest.__init__` now gathers each header's values in a list and joins them once (`django/core/handlers/asgi.py:ASGIRequest.__init__`; [Making the request: `WSGIRequest` and `ASGIRequest`](../http/request.md#from-an-asgi-scope)).

`body` checks the declared length, then measures a stream that can seek, as an ASGI request's can (`django/http/request.py:HttpRequest.body`; [The body: `body`, `POST` and `FILES`](../http/body.md#under-asgi)).

`MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input` judges by the same measure, so the same bytes sent as a file go to disk; a WSGI request's `LimitedStream` cannot seek, and there the header, which it enforces, decides (`django/core/files/uploadhandler.py:MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input`; [Multipart parsing and upload handlers](../http/uploads.md#memory-or-disk)).

At this commit the parser strips white space from each chunk, reads on while the stripped length is not a multiple of four, and joins the pieces once before decoding (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._parse`).

Under 6.0.8 the text of an element nested in a field still went into the value; since 6.1 `check_element_type` refuses a child element with content of its own with `SuspiciousOperation` (`django/core/serializers/xml_serializer.py:check_element_type`; [What changed in caching, files, signals, serialization and pagination](caching-files-signals.md)).

Past 198, the constant `MAX_GEOM_COLLECTIONS` that max_geom_collections defaults to, the reader raises `ValueError` (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKTReader.limit`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKBReader`; [Geometries in Python: GEOS and GDAL](../contrib/geometries.md#geosgeometry)).

Past 198, the constant `MAX_GEOM_COLLECTIONS` that max_geom_collections defaults to, the reader raises `ValueError` (`django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKTReader.limit`, `django/contrib/gis/geos/prototypes/io.py:_WKBReader`; [Geometries in Python: GEOS and GDAL](../contrib/geometries.md#geosgeometry)).
The notes say GeoJSON is not limited; at this commit its WKB, from GDAL, is counted at the default, whatever max_geom_collections says (`django/contrib/gis/gdal/geometries.py:OGRGeometry._geos_ptr`).
In the form field `None` keeps the default, so a model field given `None` still makes a form field that refuses past 198 (`django/contrib/gis/forms/fields.py:GeometryField.__init__`).
